taxonomy.note: Accepted by Kew as Salvia texana (Scheele) Torr.

evidence: Hays — UT Plant Resources Center Natural Purola native flora explicitly lists Salvia texana.
Travis — Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list explicitly lists Salvia texana.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County treatment.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Source-pool membership and iNaturalist counts were not used by themselves as proof.

morphology.look_here_first: Start low on the plant: look for basal leaves plus narrower cauline leaves on a short perennial. Then inspect the sharply pointed, strongly ribbed calyx and relatively small deep-violet flowers.
diagnostic_traits: both basal and cauline opposite leaves
basal leaves narrow oblanceolate to elliptic
leaf surfaces with sunken/pitted glandular hairs
terminal raceme with conspicuous leaflike bracts

confusers.separator: S. texana has basal leaves and sunken/pitted glandular hairs; S. engelmannii has only cauline leaves and conspicuous tack-shaped glandular hairs.
S. texana is a low sage; S. azurea is much taller with a long flowering axis and green calyces.
